title: Edit Airtable Record via Uploaded Audio
breadth_reason: Covers uploaded audio ASR to edit a CRM record, testing real Airtable surface verification.

v7_target.surface_rule: actual signed-in Chrome profile with Airtable
v7_target.proof_rule: fresh screenshot or DOM capture of Airtable record and workspace

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio ASR ensures audio-to-text pipeline is tested with an actual MP3 file, avoiding live mic dependency.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please update the Airtable Customers record for the Lighthouse renewal to set the status to in review and tag the owner. If you cannot prove the visible Airtable record or my signed-in workspace, decline without writing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger must generate a per-run audio artifact using the `say` command and upload it via /api/listen/upload. The audio file must be an MP3 containing the spoken reference text exactly.

success_criteria: The uploaded audio is transcribed correctly and the intent to edit the Airtable record is recognized.
The real Airtable surface (signed-in Chrome, record view) is verified and proof is captured.
If the surface is verifiable, the system performs the edit (act) or asks for confirmation (ask); if not verifiable, it declines without making changes.
The decision (act/ask/decline) is recorded with proof tied to the public user-device engine.
Secondary input modes (transcript paste, live mic) are not used; only uploaded audio is accepted.
failure_triggers: The uploaded audio is corrupted or not an MP3 file.
The surface cannot be proven because the user's Airtable tab is not visible or Chrome profile is not signed in.
The ASR output differs significantly from the spoken reference text.
The system attempts to use a fallback input mode (e.g., transcript paste) instead of the uploaded audio.
The action is performed without obtaining fresh proof of the Airtable record state.
